headline: Running for the Assembly as his own man
summary: A week before the vote, Roosevelt faces Dr. W. W. Strew, lately dismissed as head of the Blackwell's Island asylum. He tells the New York Herald he belongs to no one, and after a tense saloon stop where he scolded the owner about license fees, the district men Murray, Hess and Bullard step in to run things.

events.detail: Assembly race against Democrat Dr. W. W. Strew; election notices go out
Tells the New York Herald he will owe nothing to any boss in Albany
A saloon visit goes badly when he complains the owner pays too little for his liquor license
Murray, Hess and Bullard take charge of his campaign

tr_quotes.text: All my friends stand by me like trumps, except Al, Em + Uncle Jim.
owned by no man
untrammelled and unpledged

uncertain: Diary marker reads [DJ]; treated as diary. Murray and Hess given full names (Joe Murray, Jake Hess) from context; Bullard and 'Al, Em + Uncle Jim' not identified.

headline: Arrives in Albany and bucks the caucus

headline: Sworn in as an assemblyman

headline: Deadlock over the Speakership

tr_quotes.text: Ballotted for speaker. There are 61 Republicans in the house; there are 67 democrats, but of these 7 are Tammany Hall men, who are 'striking' for their own candidate, and so a deadlock has come about, Adjourned till Monday.
